# Project Status — PDF Utility Website

## Current state
**Crop PDF implementation and verification (2026-10-29):** Added `/crop-pdf` with local PDF.js previews and pdf-lib CropBox export; no dependencies were added. It is registered under Organize and has shared route content, instructions, FAQs, responsive/theme-aware controls, current-page crop accumulation, and an all-pages mode that applies the same relative crop to every page. Browser and synthetic-PDF checks covered drag/keyboard resizing, moving the crop area, reset, zoom and 390 px resizing, invalid replacement preservation, deletion, current-page accumulation, and all-page cropping. Exported files were independently reopened with pdf-lib and PDF.js. Three-page fixtures with different dimensions and 90° rotation, plus nonzero media/CropBox origins and 180°/90° rotations, produced crop boxes and displayed dimensions matching the selections; original content remained searchable, and restoring an original box in a test copy recovered hidden text. The tool warns that CropBox cropping does not erase outside content and that rewriting may invalidate signatures. The visible download action used `crop-pdf-fixture_cropped.pdf`; the browser bridge did not emit a download event, so the actual Downloads-folder save remains unverified. The generated Blob was captured via a temporary local receiver and independently checked. At 390 px the document remained 375 px wide; dark-theme colors and category listing were checked. `npm.cmd run build` passed with Vite 8.3.5 (2,606 modules; 1,892.05 kB minified app chunk; 1,375.83 kB PDF.js worker). The existing `docx`/`buffer` externalization and >500 kB chunk warnings remain. No lint/test scripts are configured. No commit was made.

**Edit PDF implementation (2026-10-29):** Added `/edit-pdf` using the existing pdf-lib, PDF.js, dropzone, and shared unencrypted-PDF validator; no dependencies were added. The shared registry now includes Edit PDF under Edit & Sign, and the tool has responsive controls, route metadata, instructions, FAQs, and related-tool links. The editor adds text, PNG/JPEG images, freehand strokes, highlights, rectangles, and lines as overlays; supports mark selection/movement/removal, image resizing, undo/redo, page navigation/deletion, and validated local PDF export. It explicitly does not replace existing PDF text and warns about PDF features that may be affected by rewriting. Browser testing loaded a synthetic three-page PDF, added text and a freehand stroke, deleted a page and restored it with Undo, then saved and reloaded a two-page output. A separate export included text and a generated PNG. PDF.js rendered the source text and added marks. Invalid replacement preserved the current document and showed a clear error. Keyboard-only text placement (arrows + Enter), mark selection, and movement were verified. At 390 px, the editor had no document-width overflow (375 px document width). The browser download event was not captured; generated PDF blobs were reloaded through the tool and rendered, but a saved file/standalone viewer check remains unverified. Rectangle/highlight/line, encrypted-input rejection, keyboard image placement, and dark-theme review remain unverified. No commit was made.

**OCR PDF final verification (2026-10-29):** On `/ocr-pdf`, processed a one-page image-only fixture containing `SEARCHABLE ALPHA` and `OCR VERIFY 4582`. Clicking the visible Download button saved `known-scanned_ocr.pdf` (9,704 bytes) to the Downloads folder. Playwright did not emit a download event, but the file was confirmed there and reopened through the tool's file picker; PDF.js parsed one page, extracted all five known words, and rendered the page with zero pixel differences from the source. Direct `file://` navigation was blocked by the browser's trusted-folder restriction, so the file was reopened through the app rather than a standalone viewer. A fresh-origin browser run captured successful jsDelivr responses for the Tesseract worker (31,770 bytes), relaxed-SIMD core (1,374,067 bytes), and English model (2,952,873 bytes), totaling 4,358,710 bytes (~4.4 MB); no browser page errors occurred. The selected PDF is rendered and passed to Tesseract locally; the three captured network requests were supporting assets, not the document. The worker/core are fetched from jsDelivr by default; Tesseract caches the language model in browser IndexedDB, but offline OCR is not guaranteed. Package metadata identifies Tesseract.js/core as Apache-2.0 and `@tesseract.js-data/eng@1.0.0` as MIT; model/corpus legal provenance has not been separately reviewed. Corrected the displayed asset-size and offline-use disclosure. `npm.cmd run build` passed (Vite 8.3.5; 2,604 modules; 1,840.22 kB app chunk; 1,375.83 kB PDF.js worker) and `git diff --check` passed. The `buffer` externalization and >500 kB chunk warnings predate OCR: the recorded pre-OCR build already emitted both with a 1,818.80 kB app chunk. The OCR change adds about 21.42 kB relative to that recorded build but did not introduce those warnings. No dependency or processing changes were made. A standalone-viewer test and hosting-provider log retention remain unverified.

**Unlock PDF final download check (2026-10-29):** Correct-password processing and the generated output Blob were verified in the browser, but the browser automation bridge did not expose a download event or saved file. At a requested 360 px viewport, the tab bar fit five links without internal overflow; detailed measurement is in the checklist. `npm.cmd run build` and `git diff --check` passed after this change; the existing `buffer` externalization and large-chunk warnings remain. Animated hero badges retain their existing homepage-section links. Shared category navigation, homepage cards with a bottom-up blue hover/focus tint, category-aware search, related tools, and persisted light/dark theme are implemented. Desktop animation, geometry, interactions, and themes are browser-verified. A mobile screenshot exposed clipped orbit labels; small-screen radius and label sizing were tightened, but post-fix mobile verification is pending because the browser reported a 982 px layout viewport after a 390 px resize request. The npm manifest now identifies the application accurately; its lockfile includes the approved exact `@pdfsmaller/pdf-decrypt@1.0.1` dependency without unrelated upgrades. The three direct `@types/*` development packages may be unnecessary because there are no TypeScript sources or type-check script; they were retained pending confirmation that they are not wanted for editor support. There are no lint or test scripts. Empty categories are omitted from navigation and the homepage. Ordinary PDF tools reject password-protected inputs before adding them to selected-file state; the dedicated Unlock PDF route is the authorized-password exception. Unlock PDF is registered at `/unlock` under Protect & Repair and processes locally, accepting only supported AES-256 R6/RC4 R2/R3 encryption when a correct password is supplied. Synthetic AES-256 and RC4 browser flows, wrong-password rejection, unencrypted/invalid-file rejection, page-count preservation, and password-free output parsing were verified. Browser download-event capture remains unverified. Merge PDF accepts at most five files and disables upload at the limit. Excel/PowerPoint conversion routes deliberately explain the missing local renderer rather than accepting files or pretending to convert them. PDF-to-Word and OCR PDF may fetch OCR resources from jsDelivr. The shared tool-detail hero has a category/icon/title/summary area and a separate, readable overview panel; it was browser-checked on all 16 tool routes and both Office limitation routes.

## Unlock PDF implementation — 2026-10-29
- Added the user-approved exact runtime dependency `@pdfsmaller/pdf-decrypt@1.0.1` (MIT, `pdf-lib` peer dependency) and synchronized `package-lock.json`; no unrelated package versions changed. Reviewed its published browser entry point and confirmed the implementation uses Web Crypto and PDF object parsing without a document-upload/network call. The package supports AES-256 R6 and RC4 R2/R3; AES-128 R4 is explicitly unsupported.
- Implemented `/unlock` with a separate component and registry entry under Protect & Repair. It accepts only detected encrypted PDFs, requires a user-supplied password, clears the password from UI state after each attempt, and has explicit wrong-password/unsupported/unencrypted/invalid-file messages. It does not modify the shared validator or other tools' encrypted-input rejection.
- The component decrypts in-browser, independently opens the source with PDF.js using the supplied password to count pages, then loads the output with `pdf-lib` without a password and verifies the output is unencrypted and retains the source page count. It provides a separate manual download and warns users to review signatures, forms, annotations, attachments, and specialized features because the PDF is rewritten.
- Node synthetic-fixture verification used `pdf-lib`, the installed companion encrypt package, and PDF.js: AES-256 R6 and RC4 R3 were identified; correct-password outputs reopened without a password, had two pages, and matched source extracted text; wrong passwords and unencrypted inputs were rejected.
- Browser verification on `/unlock` confirmed the route title/content; AES-256 and RC4 correct-password operations displayed verified two-page outputs; an incorrect password produced an alert and cleared the password field; unencrypted and invalid PDFs were rejected without entering selected-file state. The Protect & Repair category listed all three tools, search surfaced Unlock PDF and opened `/unlock`, and neutral info/status surfaces computed correctly in both light and dark themes. Browser download-event capture was attempted but not observed, so the final download action remains unverified.
- `npm.cmd run build`, `npm.cmd ls --depth=0`, package JSON parsing, targeted VS Code Problems checks, and `git diff --check` passed. The build emitted existing `docx`/`buffer` externalization and large-chunk warnings; the app JS chunk is 1,818.80 kB minified. A controlled before/after build was not run, so package-only bundle impact is unmeasured.
- Next: verify a real browser download and, if available, test an independently sourced AES-128 R4 fixture to confirm the documented unsupported-encryption message. Review output fidelity for PDFs with forms, annotations, attachments, and signatures.

## Unlock PDF final browser download verification — 2026-10-29
- The prior shared browser page was open at `http://127.0.0.1:5173/unlock`, but its server was stopped. Started the existing Vite dev server without rebuilding and generated a temporary two-page AES-256 R6 fixture (`ALPHA`, `BETA`; password `UnlockVerify-29!`).
- Uploaded the fixture in the browser. The Download button was absent before processing; after a correct password, the UI reported `aes256-known-password_unlocked.pdf is ready. Verified as an unencrypted 2-page PDF.`
- Invoked the Download button. The browser bridge did not report a download: `page.waitForEvent('download')` timed out after 12 seconds. Chromium CDP `Browser.setDownloadBehavior` was accepted, but no `Browser.downloadWillBegin` or `Browser.downloadProgress` events arrived. The browser tool exposes no downloaded path or file handle in this session.
- Inspected the download button's actual generated anchor metadata: filename `aes256-known-password_unlocked.pdf`, URL scheme `blob:`. Captured the underlying output Blob in the browser: 2,479 bytes, `application/pdf`, `%PDF-1.7`. Independently loaded those Blob bytes with pdf-lib (`isEncrypted: false`, 2 pages) and PDF.js (page text `ALPHA`, `BETA`). This validates the generated payload, not a file saved by the browser.
- Repeated with an incorrect AES-256 password: the expected wrong-password alert appeared, the password field cleared, and no Download button was present.
- Captured no browser console errors or page errors during the correct/incorrect workflows; the known password did not occur in captured console messages. An initial separate PDF.js inspection snippet lacked a worker URL; after setting the local Vite worker URL, the independent content check passed.
- **Outcome:** The complete user-facing download workflow remains unverified because this automation environment did not expose or save the browser download event/file. Manual completion requires clicking Download in a normal browser, confirming `aes256-known-password_unlocked.pdf` appears in its Downloads list, opening that downloaded file without a password, and confirming two pages with `ALPHA` / `BETA`.

## Watermark PDF — 2026-10-28
- Added `src/components/PdfWatermarker.jsx`, registered `/watermark` in `src/App.jsx`, and added an active matching homepage card in `src/components/Home.jsx`.
- Uses installed `pdf-lib` APIs (`drawText`, `StandardFonts.Helvetica`, `rgb`, `degrees`, and text opacity) to add centered, rotated text without rasterizing pages or changing the source file.
- Supports text, 8–96 pt size, colour, -180° to 180° rotation, 0–100% opacity, all pages, and strict 1-based page/range selection.
- Also supports independent page numbering with starting number, top/bottom placement, alignment, colour, size, margin, and an independent page range.
- Displays file size and loaded page count; supports replacing, removing, and resetting the selected file. Output page count and order are retained.
- Limitations: built-in Helvetica has WinAnsi character coverage, so unsupported text is rejected; password-protected PDFs are not supported.

## Organize, Redact, Sign, and category navigation
- Added `src/components/OrganizePdf.jsx`, `src/components/RedactPdf.jsx`, and `src/components/SignPdf.jsx`, registered their routes in `src/App.jsx`, and added their active cards to the existing category-grouped homepage.
- Organize PDF reorders, rotates, and removes pages with real previews, then uses `pdf-lib` to preserve the selected pages and produce a new document. The tested output retained two pages in reordered source order, retained text, and applied the configured 90-degree rotation.
- Redact PDF draws opaque masks and outputs rasterized pages so masked source content is not left extractable beneath a cover. Browser verification confirmed the same page count, no extracted text on the output pages, an opaque black sample mask pixel, and visible unmasked source content. Rasterization loses selectable text, vector fidelity, links, forms, and other interactive features.
- Sign PDF supports typed, drawn, and PNG/JPEG signature marks, page selection, and placement controls. Outputs are visible marks only; they do not authenticate identity, prevent document changes, or constitute certificate-backed signatures.
- Category-aware related tools render as a responsive same-category grid (excluding the current tool). Browser checks confirmed Sign shows only Watermark and Redact; Organize shows three peers under “Other organizing tools”.
- Menu dismissal, focus restoration, mobile category switching, search keyboard behavior, and homepage card focus/activation were verified; detailed evidence is in the current navigation section and checklist.
- Upload controls were checked in light and dark themes for normal, hover, focus, pressed, disabled, and simulated drag-active states. Dark menu panel and text colors were also checked; computed styles and browser evidence are recorded in the checklist.
- Unlock PDF is now implemented and registered using the approved browser-side decryption dependency. See the 2026-10-29 implementation section above for supported encryption, verification evidence, and remaining download/fidelity checks.
